DECISION AND OPINION ON REVIEW 
Timely Petition for Review under §19(b) having been filed by the Respondent herein and 
notice given to all parties, the Commission, after considering the issues of causal connection, the 
reasonableness and necessity of the medical treatment and charges, prospective medical treatment, 
temporary total disability benefits, permanent partial disability benefits, maintenance benefits, 
credits, and evidentiary and legal errors as a matter of law, and being advised of the facts and law, 
affirms and adopts the Decision of the Arbitrator, which is attached hereto and made a part hereof. 
The Commission further remands this case to the Arbitrator for further proceedings for a 
determination of a further amount of temporary total compensation or of compensation for 
permanent disability, if any, pursuant to Thomas v. Industrial Commission, 78 Ill.2d 327, 399 
N.E.2d 1322, 35 Ill.Dec. 794 (1980). 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Decision of the 
Arbitrator filed September 19, 2024 is hereby affirmed and adopted. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that this case be remanded to the 
Arbitrator for further proceedings consistent with this Decision, but only after the latter of 
expiration of the time for filing a written request for Summons to the Circuit Court has expired 
without the filing of such a written request, or after the time of completion of any judicial 
proceedings, if such a written request has been filed. 
26IWCC0139

IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent pay to Petitioner 
interest under §19(n) of the Act, if any. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent shall have credit 
for all amounts paid, if any, to or on behalf of Petitioner on account of said accidental injury. 
Bond for the removal of this cause to the Circuit Court by Respondent is hereby fixed at 
the sum of $75,000.00. The party commencing the proceedings for review in the Circuit Court 
shall file with the Commission a Notice of Intent to File for Review in Circuit Court.

WATSON FOOD CO.

An Application for Adjustment of Claim was filed in this matter, and a Notice of Hearing was mailed to each 
party.  The matter was heard by the Honorable Dennis O'Brien, Arbitrator of the Commission, in the city of 
Springfield, on June 28, 2024.  After reviewing all of the evidence presented, the Arbitrator hereby makes 
findings on the disputed issues checked below, and attaches those findings to this document. 
 
DISPUTED ISSUES 
 
A. 
 Was Respondent operating under and subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational  
 
 Diseases Act? 
 
B. 
 Was there an employee-employer relationship? 
 
C. 
 Did an accident occur that arose out of and in the course of Petitioner's employment by Respondent? 
 
D. 
 What was the date of the accident? 
 
E. 
 Was timely notice of the accident given to Respondent? 
 
F. 
 Is Petitioner's current condition of ill-being causally related to the injury? 
 
G. 
 What were Petitioner's earnings? 
 
H. 
 What was Petitioner's age at the time of the accident? 
 
I. 
 What was Petitioner's marital status at the time of the accident? 
 
J. 
 Were the medical services that were provided to Petitioner reasonable and necessary?  Has Respondent  
 paid all appropriate charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services? 
 
K. 
 Is Petitioner entitled to any prospective medical care? 
 
L. 
 What temporary benefits are in dispute?   
 
 
 TPD  
 Maintenance 
 TTD 
 
M. 
 Should penalties or fees be imposed upon Respondent? 
 
N. 
 Is Respondent due any credit? 
 
O. 
 Other  Prospective Medical

FINDINGS 
 
On the date of accident, February 15, 2018, Respondent was operating under and subject to the provisions of 
the Act.   
 
On this date, an employee-employer relationship did exist between Petitioner and Respondent.   
 
On this date, Petitioner did sustain an accident that arose out of and in the course of employment. 
 
Timely notice of this accident was given to Respondent. 
 
In the year preceding the injury, Petitioner earned $1,659.00; the average weekly wage was $414.75. 
 
On the date of accident, Petitioner was 36 years of age, married with 3 dependent children. 
 
Respondent has not paid all reasonable and necessary charges for all reasonable and necessary medical 
services.   
 
Respondent shall be given a credit of $33,141.42 for TTD, $0.00 for TPD, $0.00 for maintenance, and $0.00 
for other benefits, for a total credit of $33,141.42. 
 
Respondent is entitled to a credit of $0.00 under Section 8(j) of the Act. 
 
ORDER 
 
Petitioner’s medical conditions, a left-sided disc protrusion at L4-L5 and smaller right-sided disc 
protrusion at L5-S1, necessitating lumbar discectomy and fusion at L4-L5 and L5-S1, and resultant 
lumbar failed back syndrome are causally related to the accident of February 15, 2018.   
 
Petitioner was temporarily totally disabled as a result of the accident from February 15, 2018 through 
June 28, 2024, a period of 332 2/7 weeks, payable at $330.00 per week.   
 
All of the bills introduced into evidence in Petitioner Exhibit 35 are related to Petitioner’s left-sided disc 
protrusion at L4-L5 and smaller right-sided disc protrusion at L5-S1, necessitating lumbar discectomy 
and fusion at L4-L5 and L5-S1, and resultant lumbar failed back syndrome injuries, are reasonable and 
were necessitated to treat or cure Petitioner’s injuries suffered in this accident. Respondent shall pay said 
bills pursuant to the Medical Fee Schedule. 
 
Petitioner is entitled to prospective medical treatment as recommended by Dr. Furry, to wit, an updated 
pre-surgical lumbar MRI, evaluation of the need for potential additional surgical interventions, 
placement of spinal cord stimulator and/or pain pump and maintenance of said stimulator and pain 
pump.   
 
 
In no instance shall this award be a bar to subsequent hearing and determination of an additional amount of 
medical benefits or compensation for a temporary or permanent disability, if any.   
 
26IWCC0139

Julius Baughman vs. Watson Food Co.   18 WC 008907   
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
TESTIMONY AT ARBITRATION 
Petitioner   
Petitioner testified that he was hired by Respondent to perform the job of Machine Blender, which 
involved cutting sacks and dumping the contents into a blender. Petitioner said at the beginning of his shift on 
February 15, 2018, he found that the prior shift had left a bunch of bags in a big trash bag, and he was going to 
dump it.  He opened the door up and he guessed that when slinging the bag in, he slipped.  The next thing he 
knew he was at the hospital, having been transported there by ambulance. He said at the hospital other people 
told him what happened. Petitioner said he was discharged from the hospital on crutches, with medication 
prescribed for him.   
Petitioner testified that in the time immediately after the accident, his lower left back and hip hurt 
constantly, and the pain would radiate into his right leg, which also became increasingly numb.  He said MOHA 
sent him to physical therapy, which helped somewhat. He said the accident also affected his short term memory, 
which made answering questions during the arbitration hearing difficult, as he could not remember things he 
was asked.  
Petitioner said he was referred to Dr. Graves, who treated him with injections, which were of no benefit. 
Petitioner said he eventually had low back surgery on June 24, 2019, and that surgery helped for a while, he 
could do activities for longer periods of time, but he still had pain.  Petitioner testified that after the surgery he 
had post-operative fever and had to be readmitted to the hospital for a while. He said he continued to have pain, 
and was referred to St. Mary’s Pain Center for pain management. He said he received injections there and, prior 
to the arbitration hearing, he had surgery putting a pain pump in, with pain medicine. Petitioner testified that the 
pain pump reduced his pain tremendously, as prior to surgery he could hardly sleep, and since the surgery he 
can sleep.  
Petitioner testified that he had been referred for a potential electric stimulator for the spinal cord, and he 
was seeking coverage for his pain pump and spinal care, as he did not have the money to pay for it.  He said he 
had not worked since the time of this accident.  
 
Petitioner testified that his back pain continues as of the date of arbitration. He said if he walks for 10 or 
15 minutes his pain is quite bad and he cannot lift his leg to move. He said holding things in his arms for a few 
minutes would cause his back to hurt. He described his pain as a stabbing, burning pain. He said mowing his 
grass for 10 to 15 minutes causes his back to hurt so much he cannot do that task. He said he was on a pain 
management agreement in regard to opioid medications, and he was complying with that agreement.  Petitioner 
said that by November of 2023 he was able to stand for 20 minutes, and he had another MRI. He said he still 
planned to seek care and follow his doctor’s medical care and pain management plans, as not doing so would 
result in his not being able to function at all. He said he had an appointment with his doctor the day before the 
arbitration hearing. 
26IWCC0139

5 
 
 
Petitioner said he had undergone a functional capacity evaluation (FCE), which gave him some work 
restrictions, carrying 11 to 20 pounds from ground to waist level, and occasionally lift heavier weight. He said 
those limitations would not allow him to do his prior job, as his job with Respondent required him to pick up 50 
pound bags constantly.  He said he does go grocery shopping and does laundry, activities which cause his back 
to hurt, and he has done some work on his car, as he has a family and has to do what he has to do. He put a 50 
pound battery in his car, so it would run again.  
 
Petitioner testified that he had applied for Social Security Disability, that his claim was pending, and had 
not yet been awarded. 
On cross examination Petitioner said a co-worker told him that he had been found on the floor, non-
responsive. His fall had not been seen. He said he had not previously had treatment for his back or legs, other 
than a bump to his knee, perhaps. He then corrected himself, noting he had arthritis in his ankle and in his knee, 
and had one injection into his knee, due to swelling, and possibly one into his ankle. He said that treatment was 
not due to an injury. He was asked if he had gotten treated in 2016 for a prior knee complaint, and he said he did 
not recall having done so. 
Petitioner testified that he attempted to return to accommodated work with Respondent, being assigned 
to clean plastic roll down doors with a rag and a bucket from a scissor lift.  He said he was not provided seating 
to do the job, as you cannot sit on a scissor lift.  He said he performed the job for a few hours and realized he 
could not do that job, as he was in too much pain, so he told the company that and went home. He agreed with 
Respondent counsel that Respondent was not able to accommodate his restrictions. He said the job they offered 
him was not within his restrictions, though Respondent said it was.  
 Petitioner said that prior to working for Respondent, he had worked other types of jobs, including 
building grain bins and as a forklift driver. He said different doctors may have released him to work at different 
times, but he did not return due to his pain. He said his leg pain was in the right leg, and it went all the way 
down the leg into the foot. Petitioner said he had not previously had problems with his right foot, other than 
arthritis.  
Petitioner testified that in the period between the date of the accident and the date of his surgery, he took 
Hydrocodone for pain, but he was not taking it as of the date of arbitration, and he had difficulty remembering 
the names of the medication he had been switched to when he stopped the Hydrocodone. He said he was seeing 
a second pain management doctor as of the date of arbitration, Dr. Furry. Petitioner had difficulty remembering 
when he was taking certain medications, when he stopped taking them, and the reasons for changes of 
medication or discontinuance of medications.  
Petitioner was asked a number of questions about an archery shop and club he had participated in, 
competitions his team had won subsequent to this accident, his stopping and then changing how he participated 
in those activities, his inability to pull the bow back after this accident and his later use of a smaller bow which 
he was able to pull back.  He said he hunted prior to this accident, but had not hunted subsequent to this 
accident. He said he had gone to that shop about ten times after the accident, and had not gone there for years 
prior to the arbitration hearing. He said he might have participated in an archery competition sponsored by the 
Montgomery County Cancer Association in July of 2019, as he had done so several times.  He said the accident 
did prevent him from engaging in about 90 percent of his archery activities, but he still did about 10 percent.  
26IWCC0139

6 
 
Petitioner said he had undergone an FCE, which determined he was completely incapacitated, but he 
agreed there were still things he could do. Petitioner testified that he had attempted to find several other jobs, 
but that his pain was extreme when he engaged in any prolonged  physical activity. He said he did not keep a 
log of his applications, as most of them were online. He said he put in applications at places that were hiring 
and were not hiring, both with employers directly and by using Indeed or a similar website. He said he applied 
at fast food places, at a nursing home, wherever there was an opening.  He said he was never offered an 
interview. 
Petitioner admitted he was in a physical altercation subsequent to his accident, but he could not 
remember the date. He said his daughter and his step-daughter were at his step-daughter’s father’s house in 
Taylorville, and Petitioner received a telephone call from the step-daughter’s father, saying a pedophile had 
been offering the girls candy and trying to get them to go with him.  Petitioner went there, the man was inside a 
building, Petitioner found him, confronted him, and “lost it,” shoving the man to the ground, and going to the 
ground himself. Petitioner said he could not remember much after that, he did not know if he hit him or not. 
Petitioner said he was arrested, booked, and released as a result of this altercation.  He said he could not 
remember if in the days following that incident if he was seen by Dr. Graves for intense low back and left leg 
pain, noting his short term memory problem.  
Petitioner said he was not, as of the date of arbitration, currently looking for work, that the last 
application he had put in was approximately a month prior to the hearing, to work in a coal mine.  
Petitioner said that as of the time of the hearing he was still taking Dilaudid for pain, it was the same 
medication that was in his pain pump. He said he was taking Gabapentin, which he thought was an anti-
inflammatory, but might also help with pain.  He said he had stopped taking Norco.  
Petitioner said he was capable of sitting for prolonged periods of time.  
Petitioner said he was still being actively treated by pain management.  
On redirect examination Petitioner said that he can still shoot in archery activities, he said he had to get a 
different, smaller, bow, as he could not pull his prior bow back. He said he can pull this bow back, but 
sometimes he can shoot, and other times he cannot, depending on how his back was. He said when he shot with 
a team, his scores from early weeks in the competition were divided by the number of weeks he shot, and that 
average was what was used for the season. 
In regard to his attempt to return to work, Petitioner said there were things he could not do, such as 
bending, lifting, twisting or picking up. He said the work washing the roll down doors was not within those 
restrictions, as he had to bend, lift, twist and pick up to do that work. He said in attempting to do that he felt 
bad, and left.  
When asked about making low back and left leg complaints after the June 18, 2019 altercation incident, 
Petitioner said he had started treating at OCI in October of 2018, and had the MRI which found the disc 
protrusion, and had been seeing an orthopedist for left-sided radiculopathy before the date of that fight. He said 
his low back pain started with this injury, not with the fight.  
26IWCC0139

7 
 
On re-cross examination Petitioner testified that the smaller bow was not as hard to pull back as his 
previous larger bow had been.  He also noted that he no longer did that activity, he had gotten rid of all of his 
bows and other equipment. He said that after the fight his back did hurt worse. 
 
MEDICAL EVIDENCE 
On the date of accident, February 15, 2018, Petitioner was transported from Respondent’s plant to 
Taylorville Memorial Hospital by Dunn Ambulance. The Dunn Ambulance medics records note  that Petitioner 
was suffering from head, back, and leg pain, that neurologic symptoms were present, and that when Petitioner’s 
leg was poked, Petitioner had no reaction. (PX 2, p.7) 
 
At Taylorville Hospital on February 15, 2018, Petitioner was examined by Dr. Riesenberger, and 
complained of head pain, back pain, left leg pain, and foot pain. Dr. Reisenberger noted Petitioner was suffering 
from localized weakness in the left leg and foot, which he described as “severe.” It was further noted that  
Petitioner could not move his leg voluntarily.   CT scans did not reveal fractures or hemorrhage, though lumbar 
disc disease and facet arthropathy were observed, as were osteophyte complexes at the L3-4, L4-5, and L5-S1 
levels, which mildly narrowed the spinal canal. Petitioner’s sensation in his legs slowly returned, and he could 
move his leg, but he continued to complain of pain. Petitioner was diagnosed as having a contusion of the back, 
and was discharged in stable condition, with crutches. He was advised to return if his symptoms worsened.  (PX 
3, p.14-18) 
 
On February 17, 2018, Petitioner returned to Taylorville Memorial Hospital, complaining of increasing 
back pain and growing weakness of the left leg. He was transported by Sutton Ambulance from Taylorville 
Hospital to Springfield Memorial Hospital due to increased pain and numbness.   At Springfield Memorial 
Hospital, Dr. Cruz documented numbness on Petitioner’s left leg to his knee. An MRI was performed, and was 
interpreted to show a moderate disc bulge with focal disc protrusion abutting the thecal sac at the L4-5 level, 
along with moderate to severe neural foraminal narrowing, and a diffuse disc bulge at the L5-6 level with mild 
focal right central disc protrusion abutting the thecal sac. Petitioner was discharged with a diagnosis of back 
pain with left leg weakness. (PX 4, p.25; PX 5, p.44,46,47; PX 6, 165-167)     
 
On February 21, 2018, Petitioner was evaluated by Dr. Clem at MOHA. After an examination which 
found reduced range of motion and tenderness in the thoracic and lumbar spine, Dr. Clem diagnosed 
radiculopathy of the lumbar region, low back pain, and a contusion of the head.  Petitioner was referred to 
neurology, restricted from work and Hydrocodone was prescribed. (PX 7 p.192,193) 
 
On February 22, 2018, Petitioner was seen by Dr. Narla, who diagnosed lumbar back pain with 
tenderness over the posterior superior iliac spine area with numbness in the left leg, without significant loss of 
sensory modalities. assessed as having lumbar pain with tenderness over the iliac spine area, and numbness in 
the left leg. Dr. Narla noted Petitioner’s occipital strike to the head had not resulted in major injury other than 
headaches. Dr. Narla felt Petitioner might have an SI joint dysfunction and he was uncertain of the source of 
Petitioner’s left sided numbness. Dr. Narla prescribed Norco and Flexeril. (PX 7, p.198,199; PX 11, p.362,363) 
 
On February 27, 2018, was seen by Dr. Yociss at MOHA and was diagnosed with left sided 
radiculopathy, a head contusion, and lumbar pain.  Petitioner was referred for physical therapy, with a goal of 
26IWCC0139

8 
 
being released to work the next Monday with light duty work restrictions. Petitioner received physical therapy 
at Taylorville Memorial Hospital from February 28, 2018 through June 6, 2018.  Dr. Yociss saw Petitioner 
again on March 5, 2018, and, following some physical therapy sessions, Petitioner felt he could return to light 
duty work, using a weight limit of 25 pounds. On March 8, 2018, Petitioner called Dr. Yociss’s office and said 
he had returned to work on Tuesday, worked part of the day, and developed intense back pain again.  That same 
day, Petitioner’s physical therapist telephoned Dr. Yociess to advise that Petitioner’s pain worsened with 
therapy, and therapy was placed on hold.  On March 09, 2018, Dr. Yociss released Petitioner to work on March 
12, 2018, with no bending, and no lifting, pulling or pushing over 25 pounds. On March 13, 2018 Petitioner’s 
nurse case manager called MOHA and advised that Petitioner had decided to discontinue treatment with MOHA 
and would follow-up with his own primary care physician.  (PX 7, p.204,205,208,215, 218,219,220,222; PX 8)   
 
Petitioner was seen by Dr. Byers’s nurse practitioner (NP), Dawn Young, on March 13, 2018, and 
Petitioner noted that his wife was familiar with Dr. Graves. He advised NP Young that he had been released for 
light duty on March 6, 2018, but was only able to work half of a day, as he still had to bend frequently, 
aggravating his back. Petitioner requested a referral for a second opinion. He was referred for that second 
opinion. NP Young also restricted him from work effective March 12, 2018, and issued additional restriction 
slips thereafter. Petitioner saw NP Wright on April 13, 2018, and she recommended additional physical therapy 
and continued to restrict his work. Dr. Byers saw Petitioner May 4, 2018, with continued back complaints. It 
was noted he was trying to get into orthopedics. Subsequent off work notes extended his restrictions through 
June 15, 2018.  Petitioner subsequently participated in work hardening, and reported to NP Dawn on October 1, 
2018, that his symptoms worsened after he began the work hardening, that he had not been back to work since 
the date of his accident. On that date he also noted that he had been having radicular pain down his right leg to 
his knee for two weeks. He was to be seen by an orthopedist as conservative care had failed. (PX 11 
p.367,368,370,371,377,378,385,388,393,414) 
 
Dr. Crane examined Petitioner at Respondent’s request on April 16, 2018. He received a history of 
accident, and complaints, and performed a physical examination which revealed back pain, painful, limited 
range of motion of the low back, and normal reflexes and leg strength. He reviewed x-ray, MRI and CT images, 
all of which he found to be normal in appearance. His assessment was of low back pain.  He recommended anti-
inflammatory medication, physical therapy and limiting narcotic pain medication.  He placed restrictions in 
regard to bending, pulling, pushing, stooping , lifting no more than 10 pounds, and no overhead lifting. His 
other opinions are noted below in the summarization of his deposition testimony.  (RX 9 p.1-4) 
 
Dr. Crane examined Petitioner at Respondent’s request for a second time, on June 28, 2018.  Petitioner 
advised him that physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medication had not helped him at all, his pain was 7-
8/10. After examining Petitioner, Dr. Crane recommended Petitioner have work hardening for two weeks and 
then be reevaluated. He did not believe Petitioner was at maximum medical improvement.  (RX 9 p.7-9) 
Petitioner saw Dr. Graves on October 30, 2018, complaining at that time of bilateral back pain that 
radiated into his legs. Dr. Graves reviewed the MRI taken of Petitioner’s lumbar spine and was of the opinion 
that Petitioner had a central disc bulge at the L4-L5 level, and a smaller disc protrusion at the L5-S1 level. Dr. 
Graves said he suspected Petitioner’s left-sided L4-5 disc protrusion was causing Petitioner’s symptoms.  A 
steroid injection was performed at the L5 level on November 30, 2018. Petitioner was again seen by Dr. Graves 
26IWCC0139

9 
 
on January 29, 2019, and reported that the L5 epidural steroid injection had not helped him at all. Dr. Graves 
noted that the majority of Petitioner’s pain was back pain on the left side, and that the back pain was worse than 
Petitioner’s leg pain.  A CT scan was ordered for presurgical planning and Petitioner was directed to quit 
smoking.  (PX 10 p.275,276,278,281; PX 28, p.1859) 
Dr. Watson performed a bilateral S1 transforaminal epidural steroid injection on Petitioner on February 
27, 2019. A second injection was performed on May 15, 2019. (PX 13, p.465,466; PX 29, p.1863) 
 
Petitioner saw Dr. Graves again on April 30, 2019, and his CT scan was reviewed. The updated CT scan 
revealed a calcified herniation at the L4-5 and L5-S1 levels. Petitioner had a repeat bilateral S1 transforaminal 
steroid injection on May 15, 2019.  Dr. Graves was concerned that because most of Petitioner’s back pain was 
located in the left low back / buttock area, surgery might not completely alleviate Petitioner’s symptoms and 
Petitioner might not be completely happy with his post-surgical outcome. (PX 9, p.384,285; PX 30, p.1868) 
 
By the time Petitioner saw Dr. Graves on May 28, 2019, he reported that he had quit smoking a month 
earlier, and desired surgery if one was offered.  It was noted that a lumbar MRI had revealed foraminal stenosis 
and calcified disc herniations at L4/5 and L5/S1. A minimally invasive discectomy and fusion from L4 through 
S1 was discussed. (PX 10, p.287,288) 
 
On June 24, 2019, Dr. Graves performed an L4-L5, and L5 - S1 posterior interbody fusion at Springfield 
Memorial Hospital. Petitioner was re-admitted to Hillsboro Hospital on June 26, 2018, with a subsequent 
transfer that same day to Springfield Memorial Hospital for monitoring, for infection due to a fever. He was 
also complaining of low back pain, but noted his pre-surgery left leg radiating pain was no longer present. It 
was also felt he may have had a small pulmonary embolism infarct in the right lung base.  Postoperatively, 
Petitioner continued to complain of lumbar pain that would shoot through his legs, and an MRI then was 
performed which revealed a small amount of residual foraminal stenosis, but nothing of great concern.  At three 
months post-surgery Petitioner reported the return of some of the left leg irritation he had experienced prior to 
surgery, and medication was increased. Follow up MRI and CT scans were unremarkable, and nerve testing was 
deemed normal. On October 17, 2019, Dr. Graves was reporting that Petitioner was complaining that his pain 
had returned and was worse than it had been before surgery. Petitioner’s nerve testing was normal. (PX 10, 
p.293,295,301,304,307,309,312-315; PX 11 p.425; PX 15, p.476,477; PX 16, p.481,482; PX 18, p.815,828; PX 
19, p.848,1063; PX 21, p.1107-1109; PX 31 p.1870,1871)  
 
 Petitioner was seen by Dr. Graves on January 15, 2020, reporting that he was slowly feeling better.   Dr. 
Graves continued to wean Petitioner off pain medication and reduced the Hydrocodone dosage.  A pelvic MRI 
was performed on February 5, 2020, but no abnormalities were found other than some patchy edema oin the left 
lumbar region.  (PX 10, p.322,324,329,331; PX 21, p.1110; PX 32 p.1878)   
 
Dr. Graves referred Petitioner for pain management. On September 24, 2020, Petitioner advised Dr. 
Graves that pain management was helping to reduce some of his post-operative pain. (PX 10, p.331)  
 
A functional capacity evaluation was performed at Memorial Industrial Rehab on June 8, 2020. It was 
noted that Petitioner gave maximal effort during this testing. The assessment was that Petitioner’s perceived 
limitations were below the category of “sedentary,” but the testing indicated he was functioning a the “medium” 
Department of Labor category (21 to 50 pounds floor to waist lift and front carry), and “light” Department of

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW: 
 
In support of the Arbitrator’s decision relating to whether Petitioner’s current conditions of ill-being, a 
left-sided disc protrusion at L4-L5 and smaller right-sided disc protrusion at L5-S1, necessitating lumbar 
discectomy and fusion at L4-L5 and L5-S1, and resultant lumbar failed back syndrome, is causally 
related to the accident of February 15, 2018, the Arbitrator makes the following findings: 
The findings of fact, above, are incorporated herein. 
The summaries of medical evidence and deposition testimony, above, are incorporated herein. 
The Arbitrator’s credibility assessment, above, is incorporated herein. 
Petitioner’s low back and left leg complaints began immediately following his undisputed fall accident, with his 
making such complaints to the ambulance staff and the emergency room staff on the date of accident. Petitioner 
was subsequently diagnosed by both Dr. Graves and Dr. Furry as suffering from lumbar failed back syndrome, 
which developed directly following an L4/L5/S1 posterior interbody fusion on June 24, 2019.  The need for 
surgery was caused due to Petitioner’s disk herniations at the L4-5 and L5-S1 levels of his spine, which were, 
per Dr. Grave’s testimony, sustained or greatly aggravated by his fall of February 15, 2018, and documented in 
radiology films as well as his treating surgeon’s medical records.   Dr. Furry testified to a causal relationship of 
Petitioner’s lumbar failed back syndrome to his original work injuries and his surgery. Most recent radiology 
films revealed “incomplete ankylosis” of the intervertebral disc spaces.  Petitioner testified that he was not 
having low back or left leg problems prior to the date of his fall, and that testimony is unrebutted. Subsequent to 
the fall Petitioner has examined and treated on many occasions by his treating physicians, receiving pain and 
anti-inflammatory medication, physical therapy, steroid injections, and a two-level lumbar fusion.  A spinal 
cord stimulator trial and a pain pump trial have been recommended in efforts to treat his lumbar spine and left 
leg pain.  
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner’s medical conditions, a left-sided disc protrusion at L4-L5 and 
smaller right-sided disc protrusion at L5-S1, necessitating lumbar discectomy and fusion at L4-L5 and 
L5-S1, and resultant lumbar failed back syndrome are causally related to the accident of February 15, 
2018.  This finding is based upon the testimony of Petitioner and the treating medical records and testimony of 
Drs. Graves and Furry.  The testimony of Dr. Crane is given less weight than the testimony of Drs. Graves and 
Furry based upon their superior knowledge of Petitioner and his physical complaints and presentation over an 
extended period of time. 
The Arbitrator further finds that the chain-of-events also support a finding of causal connection.  This 
finding is based upon Petitioner’s unrebutted testimony to a pre-accident state of asymptomatic good health in 
the low back and legs, his having an accident on February 15, 2018, and his immediately after said accident
